title: Protocol for determining the regulation of lipid kinases and changes in phospholipids in vitro
protocol: Seed HEK 293T cells in 140 mm cell culture dishes.
Transfect cells with plasmid containing gene of interest with tag.
Wash cells with PBS three times and lyse in ice-cold lysis buffer.
Incubate lysates on ice for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 16,100g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash magnetic beads three times with wash buffer using a magnet.
Incubate post-nuclear supernatant with magnetic beads at 4°C on a rotating wheel for 1–2 h (time depends on the manufacturer’s instructions).
Centrifuge briefly and remove supernatant.
Wash the beads three times with wash buffer.
Mix by inverting tubes.
Add 2× Laemmli buffer with β-mercaptoethanol to 10 μL of each BSA solution.
Add 2× Laemmli buffer with β-mercaptoethanol to 10 μL of bead-bound protein.
Boil samples at 100°C for 5 minutes.
Run samples on SDS–PAGE at 100 V for 2 hours.
Incubate the gel with Coomassie Blue stain to determine the relative protein amount bound by the beads and ensure that additional bands are not present.
Wash bead-bound protein with buffers as described below.
Aliquot and store precipitated protein at −80°C if large amounts of protein have been precipitated.
Prepare phosphoinositides for the kinase assay: Mix methanol and chloroform in a 1:1 ratio.
Add the mixture to glass vials containing PI or PI(5)P lipids to create a 1 mM stock solution.
Dry off the chloroform using an argon gas flux until all liquid has evaporated, leaving a film at the bottom of the tube.
Reconstitute lipid in lipid buffer.
Sonicate twice for 30 s on ice.
Wash precipitated proteins three times with RIPA buffer.
Wash precipitated proteins twice with buffer A.
Wash precipitated proteins three times with buffer B.
Wash precipitated proteins twice with buffer C.
Incubate lipid kinase, protein kinase (10 nM), and ATP (50 μM) in assay buffer (total volume 50 μL) for 15 min at 37°C in a non-adherent tube.
Add the reaction mix to tubes containing PIs (100 μM).
Incubate the mixture for an additional 15 min at 37°C.
Stop the reaction by adding 200 μL 1N HCl.
Use the lipids directly in the next step to avoid instability when freezing phospholipids.
Store lipids in chloroform in a tightly sealed glass vial at −20°C if required.
Ensure purified kinases are as pure as possible through wash steps.
Perform SDS-PAGE for precipitated kinases and assess additional bands using Coomassie Blue stain.
Include inhibitors of the protein kinase and/or lipid kinase as controls in the assay.
Incubate inhibitors with kinases prior to initiating the kinase assay.
Use phospho-mutant and phospho-mimic forms of the lipid kinase if phosphorylation sites are known for validation purposes.
Consider using non-ionic detergents instead of SDS and sodium deoxycholate in RIPA buffer if enzyme activity is compromised.
Include negative and positive controls to ensure lack of activity is not due to buffer compositions.
Add 160 μL 1:1 chloroform:methanol to the tube containing the reaction.
Vortex and centrifuge the tube at 10,000g for 2 minutes.
Remove the upper methanol layer containing the kinases.
Wash the lower chloroform layer twice with 100 μL of 1:1 methanol:1N HCl.
Use an argon gas flux to remove excess volume.
Apply the resulting lipid solution left in the tube to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Dilute lipids in a 2:1:0.8 solution of methanol:chloroform:water in 5–8 serial dilutions starting with 100 μM.
Spot 5 μL of each dilution on the same nitrocellulose membrane as the lipids extracted from the kinase reactions.
Air-dry the membrane at room temperature for 1 hour.
Tape the membrane firmly to a flat surface to prevent curling.
Cut within the edges of the tape using a clean razor blade.
Incubate the membrane containing lipid spots in blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the membrane overnight at 4°C with 10 nM GST-ING2 protein in blocking buffer.
Wash the membrane 10 times, each for 5 minutes, with TBS-T.
Incubate the membrane with a 1:2000 dilution of anti-GST monoclonal antibody in blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the membrane 10 times, each for 5 minutes, with TBS-T.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody in TBS-T at 1:5000 dilution for 1 hour.
Wash the membrane 10 times, each for 5 minutes, with TBS-T and once for 5 minutes with TBS.
Visualize with direct infrared fluorescence detection using LICOR-Odyssey apparatus/Bio-Rad ChemiDoc.
